# Clipify full product reference

> Clipify helps Twitch creators organize clips, play highlights on stream, export videos for sharing, and publish galleries and Creator Pages.

Last reviewed: 2026-11-14

This reference describes the current application and pricing catalog. Planned roadmap items and the marketing-video compositions in the repository are not end-user product features. Current prices come from the live billing catalog, not static examples.

## Getting started and account context

- Creator signup/sign-in uses Twitch. New users get a Clipify account when they connect; returning users open their existing account. Safe saved destinations and checkout selections continue after sign-in.
- The dashboard opens the active creator or agency context. With no explicit workspace selected, the creator's own account is the default. Choosing an account changes the resources and permissions in use; the next page does not silently replace that selection.
- The sidebar provides Home, Streams, Clip Inventory, Overlays, Playlists, Galleries, Runner, Clip layouts, Tools and Settings where permitted. Home shows recent clip performance and setup next steps. Existing clips do not mean OBS setup is complete.
- Invited team/agency members can have account access without a creator plan of their own. The invitation and recovery screens support their appropriate sign-in methods; the public creator signup remains Twitch-based.
- Admin View is a separate, visibly identified support context. It is not a creator-facing collaboration or account-sharing feature.

## Clip inventory, streams and cache

- Clip Inventory supports searching known clips, date/category/view/duration filters, sorting, preview and selection. Stream detail narrows the same workflow to one stream.
- Streams provides recent stream history and clip performance. Counts describe the available cached clips, not proof that every Twitch clip has already been retrieved.
- Clip synchronization includes incremental work and historical backfill. Account settings show cache coverage, recent sync status, refresh availability and scheduled crawl work. A refresh request starts background work; inspect status instead of claiming immediate completion.
- Clip searches and exports can require renewed Twitch authorization, and unavailable/deleted provider clips can be skipped with an explanation.

## Clip inventory, exports and reusable layouts

- Original downloads remain untouched. Desktop exports use landscape 16:9 compositions; Mobile exports use portrait 9:16 compositions.
- Save reusable layouts with Desktop and Mobile versions. Arrange and crop gameplay and camera layers; add titles, channel/clipper information and a logo. Account brand styling supplies shared colors, fonts and corners for layouts and overlays.
- Manual exports and layouts are available on Free and Pro. Free Desktop/Mobile exports include a Clipify watermark; Pro can remove it. Original downloads are not branded or recomposed.
- One output downloads as MP4; multiple outputs download as a ZIP of videos without a metadata sidecar. The export queue shows progress, skipped-file reasons, cancellation and retry. Keep the browser tab open while processing.
- General, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram Reels, Reddit, Discord and custom-size presets prepare downloadable files. Discord options distinguish upload allowances. A preset is not an automatic upload or a guarantee that a platform will accept a file.
- Composed exports depend on browser/device capabilities. Unsupported conversion, authorization failures and size constraints have local recovery feedback. Retry does not require rebuilding the whole clip selection.
- Start at https://clipify.us/features#exports, then Clip Inventory, a stream's clips, or Clip layouts in the dashboard. Automated social publishing and social-post scheduling are not included.

## Browser-source overlays and playback

- Save an overlay, then add its private URL as a browser source in OBS Studio, Streamlabs, XSplit or comparable software. No local plugin or Runner is required for this workflow.
- Use separate overlays for BRB, Starting Soon, Ending or other scenes within plan limits. Changing the saved clips/settings does not require replacing the source URL.
- Sources include all-time clips, supported recent periods, featured clips, reusable playlists and the Viewer Queue. Filtering can use dates, duration, views, title words, clip creators and Twitch categories; advanced controls require the relevant plan.
- Free supports Random playback. Pro adds Top and Smart Shuffle. Playlist order is available for playlist sources. A configured source with no matching clips can remain idle.
- Account brand styling is shared across overlays and clip layouts. Pro Theme Studio additionally arranges clip/channel information, timers, progress elements, typography and appearance effects.
- Private OBS URLs grant access to an overlay. Do not publish them as public website embed links or expose them in public documentation.

## Playlists, Viewer Queue and live control

- Playlists are independent saved clip selections reusable across overlays. Add/remove clips and reorder a handpicked selection. Counts and limits come from the generated plan comparison below.
- Pro on-demand imports let the creator review filtered discovery and append to or replace a playlist. This is a requested import, not an automatic daily playlist-publishing service.
- Pro includes the remote panel, configured Twitch chat commands and channel-point integration. Supported live actions include play/pause, skip, mute/volume, visibility and queue operations.
- A connected Twitch Channel Points reward can let viewers submit clip links for the Viewer Queue, subject to configured queue/source rules. Twitch reward eligibility and permissions still apply.
- The remote panel is usable from another screen. A queued command or stale player report does not prove that OBS received or played the requested clip.

## Website galleries, Clip Player and Clipify Elements

- Galleries use curated playlists or live clip sources. Live resolution can use newest/most-viewed selection; advanced filters, themes and runtime styling depend on the plan.
- Free includes one branded gallery with up to 50 live results; Pro supports unlimited galleries and up to 100 live results per gallery. The generated pricing comparison is authoritative for plan availability.
- Install Clipify Elements once, then place supported custom elements on the website. A gallery uses `<clipify-gallery gallery-id="GALLERY_ID"></clipify-gallery>`.
- Raw gallery iframes are unsupported because gallery playback/modal coordination belongs to the host page. Individual Clip Player embeds support Clipify Elements or the supported public `/embed/` iframe workflow.
- Free gallery attribution is included; Pro can choose whether to show it. Public preview/embed links and private streaming-source links serve different purposes.
- Installation guide: https://help.clipify.us/hc/clipify/articles/install-clipify-elements.

## Creator Pages and community discovery

- Free and Pro include a shareable Creator Page with creator details and browsable, playable Twitch clips.
- Page availability and discovery are separate settings. A disabled page is unavailable; an unlisted page remains accessible by direct URL but is excluded from search/Clipify discovery and the sitemap.
- Pro includes Creator Page traffic and clip-engagement analytics, acquisition/location/device/browser/OS breakdowns, CSV downloads and supported social-preview title/description customization.
- Community is the public directory of eligible discoverable creators. It has name/username search, group tabs and distinct profile/Twitch links. Live and membership indicators do not grant permissions or a paid plan.
- Public URLs can be shared in Twitch panels, Discord, social profiles and websites. Keeping a page unlisted is not a substitute for access control over private OBS sources.

## Team and agency access

- Creator owners can invite collaborators and use preset/custom permissions. Team access and custom roles are managed in Settings → Team and the relevant role/invitation screens. Pro collaboration does not require sharing the owner's login.
- Agency workspaces provide creator links, member permissions, billing and creator-seat allocations. Creator access requires an accepted, active relationship and the allowed permissions; selecting an agency does not grant unrestricted access to every creator.
- A valid agency creator-seat allocation can provide effective Pro access. Revocation, suspension or expiry affects future operations. Agency billing is separate from a creator's personal subscription.
- The standalone paid Runner product and agency Runner-seat product are retired. Do not recommend purchasing a separate Runner entitlement.

## Self-hosted Runner and broadcasting

Runner is included with Free and Pro, with unlimited streaming hours on your own computer. Advanced Runner features require effective Pro, including valid Pro grants, trials, and agency creator seats.

- Runner is optional software on the creator's own Windows, Linux or macOS computer. Clipify coordinates it; Clipify does not host its compute or guarantee that the user's computer stays online.
- Free allows one active broadcast across devices and one destination, with manual clip playback or live-input fallback. Registering another device does not add another active Free broadcast.
- Free generated clips/standby include Clipify attribution. The normal incoming live feed is not watermarked by Runner. Pro adds multiple destinations, independent broadcasts, schedules, custom standby and watermark removal, subject to hardware and bandwidth.
- Saved destinations belong to the creator and can be reused by devices. Twitch/YouTube connections and manual stream keys are supported. Each destination consumes upload bandwidth.
- Pro schedules support local/saved timezones, recurring occurrences and edits to one or following occurrences. Future scheduling and past/current broadcast details have different editing rules. Scheduled stops finish the current clip.
- Scheduling can set supported stream details, including titles, Twitch categories and YouTube descriptions/thumbnails. Provider streaming/metadata permissions are separate from normal Clipify sign-in.
- Initial setup provides platform downloads, enrollment and manual instructions for headless use. A device must connect before configuration/health is available. Snapshots/previews may wait for a fresh frame or require retry.
- Keep the device and connectivity available. Missing stream credentials, a disconnected Runner or expired permissions require recovery before a broadcast can run. Credentials and stream keys are not public status data.

## Settings, security and privacy controls

- Settings groups Account, Brand styling, Connections, Creator Page, Billing and Team, subject to permissions.
- Account settings include verified email/security management, clip-cache status, privacy preferences and account data/deletion actions. Passkeys and email-code access are managed through security/recovery screens; this does not add a password signup form to the public creator login.
- Connections lists linked Twitch/Google accounts, connected AI apps and AI-app activity. Removing a provider can also remove its Runner channel connection. The required primary Twitch identity cannot be disconnected as a way to bypass creator sign-in requirements.
- Some sensitive account/provider actions require fresh identity verification. A failed or cancelled verification does not complete the requested action.
- Request account-data exports and deletion through Account settings. Export links are time-limited. Deletion can be scheduled around paid access or requested immediately, with a 30-day recovery period before permanent erasure. These controls are separate from downloading Twitch clip videos.
- Privacy preferences are available in Settings → Account, the public footer and Cookie Policy. Basic cookieless Umami traffic statistics run independently of optional consent. Statistics consent enables account-linked product analytics, engagement, browser performance and public-page heatmaps; functionality consent enables support chat. Withdrawal stops new optional collection and preserves basic pageviews.
- Consent choices are maintained by the consent service. Clearing browser storage is not the account-level withdrawal control. See the Privacy/Cookie policies for data categories, legal bases and retention.

## Membership, member cards and badges

- Accounts can have a stable member number and member-since date. Member cards provide a shareable public identity with supported badges.
- Card URLs use non-guessable identifiers rather than usernames. Share through supported system/social actions or download a rendered PNG.
- Recognition badges are not subscription plans. Some reflect an active qualifying status; others are lasting recognition. The current catalog is generated from the application registry:

{{BADGE_CATALOG}}

## Plans, trials and billing

- Free continues without a paid subscription. Eligible new creators receive seven days of temporary Pro access without a card; eligibility and effective entitlements come from the account, not simply its age.
- A valid trial, grant or agency seat can provide effective Pro features. It is not the same as a paid subscription or recorded revenue.
- Pro has monthly/yearly billing. Live prices, promotions and availability come from https://clipify.us/pricing. Billing settings support the currently available plan changes, cancellation/reactivation and billing-provider flows.
- A checkout click is not a completed payment. Valid selections are retained for retry after recoverable checkout failures; unavailable/invalid selections return to plan selection.
- Current feature availability below is generated from the same catalog as the pricing page:

{{PLAN_COMPARISON}}

## AI assistant access (MCP)

- Connect compatible clients to `https://clipify.us/mcp` using OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE. Metadata/scopes are discovered from the endpoint; supported public clients can register their callbacks dynamically.
- Users approve accessible creators and Read, Write or Custom permissions. Write can include requested deletion permissions. An operation must be requested, approved and allowed by the current creator/team/agency permissions and plan; registration alone grants no access.
- Private OBS links and Runner credential rotation require their specific approved permissions. Keep private URLs out of public website snippets. Clients do not receive the browser session, Twitch access tokens or broadcast stream keys.
- Connections settings show approved apps, permissions and activity, and let users revoke access. Revoked credentials cannot continue operating. Client-side warning labels do not replace backend checks.
- The public catalog contains {{MCP_TOOL_COUNT}} tools. Use focused overlay/gallery settings, source, filters, playback and theme operations. Partial edits preserve omitted values and require current revisions where specified.
- Live control uses the public named actions such as `play_overlay`, `pause_overlay`, `skip_overlay` and `set_overlay_volume`. The broad `control_overlay`, `update_overlay`, `update_gallery` and `get_overlay_embed` helpers are internal, not public MCP tools.
- Search/resolve clips, preview imports and commit the exact reviewed selection. Incomplete discovery needs narrower filters. Free limits still apply; filtered bulk import requires Pro.
- Public website snippets use `get_gallery_embed` or `get_player_embed`; private OBS source URLs use `get_overlay_link` with its separate permission.
- Runner workflows cover setup, configuration, stream sessions, commands and available snapshots. Installation/enrollment and missing provider credentials still require the supported user/device flow.
- Feedback submission is only for an explicit user-requested report with confirmation. It returns a queued receipt, not proof that support has read it. No transcript, screenshot or replay is attached automatically.
- Video-file exports, billing changes, team/security administration and AI marketplace submissions are outside this MCP tool set. Named AI-host support depends on that host's remote MCP/OAuth implementation.
